title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation  [ the process of becoming like Jesus] part 18
scripture_text: ‘’Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word should share all good things with their instructor. Do not be deceived God cannot be mocked. A man reaps what he sows. Whoever sows to please their flesh from the flesh will reap destruction; whoever sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life. Let us not become weary in doing good for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up. Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers.’’
devotional:
Seeds of perseverance. Galatians 6:9

We need not to become weary in doing good. Sometimes in life we get weary, tired, burned out. To be weary is to feel empty of a fighting spirit, to cease to fight for what is right, to become exhausted as a result of giving in to evil. - literally, “Let us not keep on giving in to evil while doing good." Paul is telling us to keep on doing good, even if you feel that you are wasting your time, or if you feel that it is pointless. To sow good seed is to, keep on doing good in the face of evil and opposition, because good seed will produce a good harvest. Sometimes we become tired, we lose perspective, and we give into feelings of discouragement.

The word for good means beautiful, handsome, excellent, eminent, choice, surpassing, precious, useful, suitable, commendable, admirable. When we become weary, and feel like giving up, we should decide to choose to sow good seed, go and do something that is beautiful, excellent, etc.

Paul continues by saying for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up. Often giving up is more a mental attitude and a negative emotion that can lead to physical exhaustion. We can lose our vision, our purpose, our enthusiasm and drive and before long we have ceased to sow the good seed that is consistent with living a godly life.

Seeds of love. We need to be people that does good to all.

Paul ends this section by giving two general principles for sowing good seed.

[a] Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people. Three times in these verses Paul uses the word good. The word “all,” pas, means to each and every person, regardless of who or what they are; it doesn’t matter if they’re Protestant, it doesn’t matter if they’re Catholic, it doesn’t matter if they’re Muslim, it doesn’t matter. You do good to all men, regardless of any prejudice, regardless of whether they’re believers or unbelievers. It doesn’t matter; you do good to all men. Maybe making the most out of life is about seeing it as a continual opportunity to do good to others. Imagine going into life with that attitude. The goodness that Paul is referring to is based upon a person’s character, it is a spontaneous expression of who they are.

Seeds of responsibility, especially to those who belong to the family of believers. Galatians 6:10

We have responsibility to the family of God. The word for family oikeios, refers to all the participants of a particular family. It carries the idea of belonging to a place of safety. If we are going to be an authentic expression of the life of God, then our lives must become a safe place for others. If we recognise others as part of our family, then we are going to be proactive in sowing seed that will produce life. We need to be people who demonstrate continual care for others.

‘Sowing to please the Spirit means "serving one another in love" (5:13), restoring one who has been caught in sin (6:1), carrying the burdens of others (6:2), giving generously to those who teach in the church (6:6) and doing good to all (6:9). Sometimes sowing to the Spirit has been defined in terms of private, personal holiness, as if it were something done in a closet by oneself. But sowing to the Spirit in the context of Paul's teaching here involves building love relationships with others. Sowing to the Spirit cannot be done in isolation or separation from others. Carrying the burdens of others requires in-depth participation in their pain and sorrow. As we see in verse 9, sowing to the Spirit means doing good to others. If sowing to the sinful nature means selfish indulgence, then sowing to the Spirit means selfless service. IVP Commentary

Every one of us are people of potential, there are lots of things we cannot do, control, or change, often circumstances are beyond our ability to do anything about, but the one thing we are all responsible for is the people we are becoming, the character we are developing into. In our passage, Paul promises that if we sow to the Spirit we will reap eternal life. This does not mean that eternal life is earned by what we do, it does mean though that eternal life is experienced as we sow to the Spirit. We often make the mistake in thinking that when the bible speaks about eternal life it is talking about life in heaven, but it’s not. Eternal life is best understood as experiencing the very life of God in the present, it has more to do with the quality of our lives, than its longevity. The longevity of eternal life is only part of its quality, but it is not its essence. Eternal life is experiencing the reality of God in the here and now. Eternal life is about becoming the people we are meant to be, the people God wants us to be.

I wonder will we make it?
prayer: Father may I be totally faithful till my last breath.
